body.x: SOLVIT System (CEO Yeong-Goo Kim) is making waves at CES 2025 with its award-winning intelligent search and rescue system, SOLVIT-iSAR. Recognized with a CES 2025 Innovation Award in the Smart City category, this groundbreaking solution addresses the challenges of locating individuals in communication dead zones, attracting global buyers and visitors alike.

SOLVIT-iSAR combines radio wave analysis with intelligent reasoning to detect missing persons in areas without conventional communication signals. By reducing search zones by up to 1/25 and automating manual data analysis processes that typically take over three hours to just 10 minutes, the technology offers a transformative approach to securing the golden hour in rescue operations.

The system uses communication records and time-diffusion models to predict precise search locations, leveraging radio data to reflect the movement patterns of those in distress. This approach significantly enhances accuracy, paving the way for efficient rescue missions in rural, mountainous, and low-signal environments and mobile device battery depletion cases.

body.cap: Live demonstration of the SOLVIT-iSAR system in action | Photo by AVING News

body.x: The CES booth provided live demonstrations of SOLVIT-iSAR’s capabilities, showcasing how the system identifies a person’s last known signal and pinpoints their location even in signal-dead zones. The compelling demos resonated strongly with global buyers, with one stating, “SOLVIT System’s technology offers a realistic and innovative solution to a critical problem. If adopted globally, this could save countless lives.”

Additionally, SOLVIT System showcased how the technology adapts to specific scenarios, including weak signal areas in rural regions, mountain rescue operations, and emergency response in remote environments. This versatility has sparked interest from emergency response organizations in the U.S., Europe, South America, and Africa.

body.cap: SOLVIT System booth at CES 2025 | Photo by AVING News

body.x: SOLVIT-iSAR's innovation was further validated by its CES Innovation Award in the Smart City category. CEO Yeong-Goo Kim remarked, “We are honored to have our solution recognized globally for addressing rescue blind spots in communication dead zones. This exhibition marks a significant step in showcasing our technology and fostering collaborations with global institutions to advance regulatory and technological support.”

Kim expressed gratitude to local fire and police departments for their support during the system’s development and the Korea Communications Agency (KCA) for providing access to radio resource information. “We look forward to meeting more partners at CES and setting new standards in the global rescue market,” he added.
